name: Frank Lampard
blurb: Scored 177 Premier League goals, the most by a midfielder in the competition's history, and captained Chelsea to the 2012 Champions League.
hints: Born in Romford, London. His father played for West Ham and his uncle is Harry Redknapp.
Came through West Ham's youth team and had a loan spell at Swansea City in 1995.

name: Sergio Aguero
blurb: His last-minute winner against QPR in 2012 gave Manchester City their first English title since 1968.
hints: Born in Buenos Aires. He debuted for Independiente aged 15 years and 35 days.
He was married to the youngest daughter of Diego Maradona.

name: Eric Cantona
blurb: Won four Premier League titles in five years with Manchester United after joining from Leeds for £1 million in 1992.
hints: Born in Marseille. He made his senior debut for Auxerre in 1983.
After football he turned to acting, starting with a role in the 1998 film Elizabeth.

name: Ryan Giggs
blurb: Won 13 Premier League titles, more than any other player, and made a club-record 963 appearances for Manchester United.
hints: Born in Cardiff. As a schoolboy he played under the surname Wilson.
He captained England Schoolboys before choosing to play for Wales.

name: Sergio Ramos
blurb: Spain's most-capped player with 180 caps, and scorer of the 93rd-minute equaliser in the 2014 Champions League final.
hints: Born in Camas, near Seville, and came through Sevilla's academy.
Joined Real Madrid in 2005 for €27 million, a record for a Spanish defender.

name: Gianluigi Buffon
blurb: Won 176 caps for Italy, the most of any goalkeeper, and holds the Serie A appearance record.
hints: Born in Carrara, Tuscany. He made his Serie A debut for Parma aged 17.
In 2001 Juventus paid a world-record fee for a goalkeeper to sign him.

name: Andrea Pirlo
blurb: A World Cup winner with Italy in 2006, he also won the Champions League twice with AC Milan.
hints: Born in Flero, Italy. He made his Serie A debut for Brescia aged 16.
Chipped a Panenka penalty in Italy's Euro 2012 quarter-final shoot-out win over England.

name: Luis Suarez
blurb: Scored 31 Premier League goals for Liverpool in 2013–14 and won the European Golden Shoe twice.
hints: Born in Salto, Uruguay, and started at Nacional.
His first European club was Groningen in the Netherlands.

name: Karim Benzema
blurb: Won the 2022 Ballon d'Or and five Champions League titles with Real Madrid.
hints: Born in Lyon and came through his hometown club's academy.
Joined Real Madrid in 2009.

name: Robert Lewandowski
blurb: Broke Gerd Müller's Bundesliga record with 41 goals in 2020–21, and is Poland's all-time top scorer.
hints: Born in Warsaw. He joined Borussia Dortmund from Lech Poznań in 2010.
Scored five goals in under nine minutes against Wolfsburg in 2015.

name: Bukayo Saka
blurb: Named England Men's Player of the Year for both 2021–22 and 2022–23.
hints: Born in Ealing, London, to Nigerian parents.
Joined Arsenal's academy at the age of seven.

name: Jude Bellingham
blurb: Won the Golden Boy award in 2023 and was named La Liga Player of the Season in his first year at Real Madrid.
hints: Born in Stourbridge. He became Birmingham City's youngest first-team player at 16.
Birmingham retired his No. 22 shirt when he left for Borussia Dortmund in 2020.

name: Roy Keane
blurb: Captained Manchester United to the treble in 1998–99.
hints: Born in Cork. Nottingham Forest signed him from Cobh Ramblers in 1990.
Joined Manchester United in 1993 for a British record fee of £3.75 million.

name: Son Heung-min
blurb: Shared the 2021–22 Premier League Golden Boot with Mohamed Salah and lifted the Europa League with Tottenham in 2025.
hints: Born in Chuncheon, South Korea. His first European club was Hamburg.
Won the 2020 Puskás Award for a solo goal against Burnley.

name: Marcus Rashford
blurb: Scored twice on his Manchester United debut in 2016 and was made an MBE in 2020 for his campaign against child food poverty.
hints: Born in Manchester. He joined Manchester United's academy at the age of seven.
Became the youngest Englishman to score on his international debut, against Australia in 2016.

name: Edwin van der Sar
blurb: Saved Nicolas Anelka's penalty to win the 2008 Champions League final shoot-out for Manchester United.
hints: Born in Voorhout, Netherlands, and started his senior career at Ajax.
Played for Juventus and Fulham before joining Manchester United.

name: Petr Cech
blurb: Kept 202 Premier League clean sheets, the most in the competition's history.
hints: Born in Plzeň. He played for Sparta Prague and Rennes before Chelsea.
Wore a rugby-style headguard after fracturing his skull in 2006.

name: Jamie Vardy
blurb: Scored in 11 Premier League games in a row in 2015–16, the season Leicester City won the title.
hints: Born in Sheffield. Sheffield Wednesday released him at 16.
Played non-league for Stocksbridge Park Steels, Halifax and Fleetwood before Leicester.
